messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: My development activity after v2.10.0
parts:
0. I'm looking forward to tagging Math v2.10.0 and Stan v2.10.0. We should be able to tag both asap. We are currently waiting on 1 thing:
  - Math: review of a pull request that fixes the binomial_coefficient_log bug from rstan:: https://github.com/stan-dev/math/pull/273

Michael's implementation of the stiff solver will be in the next release. I haven't looked at how that's exposed through the language. I think we should look at that before v2.10.0 is released since I think we have a clearer idea of how we want to expose the integrate_ode_* functions in the language. We've already swapped out CVODE for CVODES here.

Sebastian's new stiff solver implementation will not be in the next release. It needs a bit more work and I need to review the tests. I haven't even checked to see if it's instantiated in the ways Stan would instantiate it.


1. After v2.10.0, the core libraries are going to move around. Right now we have two core libraries:
- Stan: stan-dev/stan
- Math: stan-dev/math

Stan is now going to be split into language, algorithms, services. I forget if we decided to abbreviate or not, but it should look like:
- language: stan-dev/language
- algorithms: stan-dev/algorithms
- services: stan-dev/services
- math: stan-dev/math

There are two main concerns I have: 1) making it easy on the developers and 2) keep some sort of history and leave the builds relatively intact.

I think if we renamed the stan-dev/stan repo, GitHub will help us out and track the submodule through the name change. I think stan-dev/stan should be renamed to stan-dev/language and we can copy the repos into algorithms and services.

Questions:
- if we wanted to do abbreviations, what should they be? lang, alg, api?
- should stan-dev/stan be renamed to algorithms instead of language?

Any major objections? This will take a little bit of work, but I think it's for the best. Here's how the dependencies will work:

rstan/pystan/cmdstan -> services  ->  algorithms  -> math
                                  ->  language

Math won't need to be touched. (Sebastian and Rayleigh, this means the work you're doing won't be affected at all.)

Mike, hopefully this doesn't mess up your world. If you've pushed to branches, I can try to move all the branches over. That make sense to you?


2. Full logging instead of streams.
Once we break apart the Stan repo, we can then implement full logging with logging levels. See https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Consolidated-Output-for-Sample,-Optimize,-ADVI,-and-Diagnose

This means we can be consistent with our output from the core library and we can use structured output so rstan's output can be controlled easily.

This will also help Krzysztof with what he's implementing with databases and other outputs.




3. Services. This is the biggie. This will take most of the duplicated code out of cmdstan, rstan, and pystan.

(Mike, you were right about having a consolidated config. The implementation wasn't and I was too caught up in the details. Bob sketched out something that will work. I can implement it cleanly and I want to push so this can happen very quickly.)

I'm pretty sure I know how all the pieces fit, so I'm ready to move forward and replace everything. The overall interfaces won't change, but the backend will be a lot easier to manage.



Any objections? Any suggestions? Anyone want to help?




Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] My development activity after v2.10.0
parts:
There are several pieces to the new interface design:

readers
writers
services

The services are the facade for the algorithms like NUTS and L-BFGS
(I think that's what Michael and Daniel have been calling
"routes", but I'm not 100% sure). The services involve readers and
writers as callbacks. They shouldn't require any Boost or Eigen data
structures.

The services design will be very similar to Michael's
original plan in its client-facing API.

I don't know if there are any Eigen types left in the readers/writers.

Sticking to C++ is easy for 1D containers, but not so
good for 2D structures. But most (all?) of those are going to be
encapsulated in the readers/writers (I don't think user-supplied
mass matrices will land in the first version).

We won't be moving to C++11 until our interfaces can
cope.

We'll still need Boost and Eigen on the back end.

- Bob

The specific list I could help on is something like: 1) pulling CmdStan through this process; 2) anything with the writers; 3) taking the current output spec you link to and proposing a key-value version; 4) replacing the reader(s) once we have a solid output spec; and 5) code review on any of the above.
